          Upgrade path unchanged from 3.3.7: the update package accepts a node on 3.3.3 or newer. A node on 3.3.2 or older applies satom-update-3.3.3.tar.gz (release v3.3.3) first, then this one.

          The upgrade creates the Python Studio tables (migration studio01) and installs new versions of satom-scripts.service and satom-integrations.service, which now carry resource limits (memory, tasks, CPU, a memory-backed /tmp). A site whose scripts need more raises them in a systemd drop-in.

          Added

          • Python Studio → Examples: working examples of every Studio piece, installed with one click, as asked: "put examples of everything in that section; you can use the FortiGate API to look up a rule as an example, and NetBox things". Four bundles, written against the answers a FortiGate 8.0.1 and NetBox 4 actually give:
          • FortiGate: which rule lets this traffic through? — an app built only from the diagram: the route back to the source (monitor/router/lookup), the FortiGate's own policy-lookup, the matching rule from cmdb/firewall/policy, two decisions, and actions on the verdict (save to a data store, download CSV, ask for the access as a change request); the same lookup as a Script Library script.
          • NetBox: who owns this IP address? — a script that calls a connection, and an app whose diagram runs that script.
          • Explain a flow — one script with two connections (FortiGate and NetBox).

          • Data stores: site contacts — no external system: a list field fed by a data store, a query and an upsert, published at once. Ids start with ex-; installing never overwrites an object you edited, and removing keeps what something else still uses. Connections are created without a secret and pointed at a placeholder host, so nothing reaches a device until their setup is finished. The console gained two examples in a Studio group (the fleet as CSV for a data store import; every FortiGate with the base URL of a connection to it). User guide §23.8.

          • Python Studio apps (Python Studio → Apps): asked for as "the user can create their own database, their own process defined with a diagram, add forms, and receive an output they can act on; the administrator creates them and they appear in Operations → Plugins, each with its own menu entry".

          • An app is a form, a diagram and an output. The form has text, number, date, checkbox, password and list fields; a list can take its choices from a data store column or from an API. The diagram is drawn in the same editor as Process, with app steps: Set a variable, Decision, Fail, Output, Read / Write a data store, Query a database (PostgreSQL), Call an API, Run a script (the published Script Library version). Steps read the form and earlier results through sandboxed templates ({{ form.host }}, {{ rows }}); an undefined name is an error, not an empty value. A step ends ok or error (a decision yes or no); an error follows only an error arrow, never "always", so a flow does not carry on with data it never got.
          • Publishing freezes a version. The menu entry and every run use it until the next Publish; editing the draft changes nothing for users. A draft with problems (no Start, an arrow to nowhere, a form field the diagram reads but the form lacks) cannot be published. Test runs of the draft can be a rehearsal: steps that write are described, not executed.
          • Where and who are the author's choice: the ADOMs it appears in (in Global, under Global → Plugins), and the groups or people who may use it, plus every Python Studio author. Nobody else sees the entry or can open the app, its runs or their actions (404).
          • Actions on the output (buttons under a finished run): save to a data store, download CSV or JSON (spreadsheet-safe), send to a connection, run another app with the output, or raise a change request. A change to a device is never made from an app: it becomes a DRAFT change request through the existing create path and waits for the normal approval.
          • Runs execute in the background and the page follows them; password values are masked in every run record; a run left "running" by a service restart is reported as interrupted.
          • Groups (Administrator → Access → Groups): named sets of users, managed with the user-management key. Apps are shared with groups or people; a group an app is shared with cannot be deleted (409, names the apps).
          • Data stores (Python Studio → Data stores): tables defined in the UI with typed columns (text, number, boolean, date, json); rows are added, edited and deleted by hand or by apps, filtered, and exported / imported as CSV (the import is all-or-nothing, the export spreadsheet-safe). No SQL or DDL is reachable from the UI and a data store cannot reach any other SATOM table; a schema change never deletes stored values. They live in the SATOM database, so they replicate to the standby and travel in every backup and clone.

          • Connections (Python Studio → Connections): external HTTP APIs (none, basic, bearer, API key in a header, OAuth2 client credentials) and external PostgreSQL databases (read-only unless a step allows writes). Every call stays under the base URL: absolute URLs, //, .. and backslashes are refused and redirects are returned, never followed; a step cannot set the credential header. The secret is write-only, kept in the vault or encrypted by the vault mode, redacted out of errors, and the vault migrate / scrub actions cover it. A Test button tries a call and a JSON path. Script Library scripts call the connections they declare with satom_script.connection("crm").get(...) (or .query(...) for PostgreSQL): the scripts runner makes the call outside the sandbox and adds the credential, which reaches it only as a single-use wrapped vault token, so the script never holds it.

          • Python Studio (Administrator → Studio) joins the Script Library and the Python Console in one page, as asked: "join the script library and the python console in a single studio". An Explorer on the left switches between the Scripts pane (the library list) and the Console pane (the sandboxed console over the curated datasets) and opens any script in its editor. The script editor gained a Console tab, to try code against the fleet data without saving it in the script. One menu entry replaces the two. Each pane keeps its own permission key and its own sandbox: the page opens for a holder of studio.script_library or studio.python_console, and the console never runs for a profile that only holds the library key. New addresses: /studio/, /studio/scripts/…, /studio/console/run; the old /database/py-console and /database/scripts/… addresses redirect (308 keeps the method and the body of an old POST).

          • Settings → User Interface → Appearance → Import from a site… builds a theme from somewhere else, as a new theme that is not applied until you review it and press Apply. Asked for as "a button to take a template from another site: the logo, the colours, the left sidebar".

          • Another SATOM node: its address plus an API token minted there with the read scope. The theme arrives exactly as it is there, logo and favicon included: the active theme, or the one named. The token is used for that one request and is not stored. New endpoints GET /api/v1/ui/theme and GET /api/v1/ui/themes (read).
          • A website: its brand colour (from theme-color, a brand-named CSS variable, or the most used colour) becomes the accent, sidebar, top bar, gradients and glows, and a dark header/navigation becomes the sidebar. Its square icon becomes the logo and its favicon the favicon. Every audited colour pair is pushed to 4.5:1. The layout, page canvas, text colours and font stay SATOM's. A report lists where each value came from.
          • The node fetches only http(s) URLs with no credentials in them. It refuses loopback, link-local (cloud metadata), multicast and reserved addresses, re-checks every redirect, never sends a token to a redirected host, verifies TLS against the trust store and caps every size. Internal sites are allowed.

          Fixed

          • A required text column of a data store could be blanked with an empty string (only a missing value counted as missing).

          • In the Global ADOM a profile that held only studio.script_library (and not user_manage) saw no Studio group at all, so its one tool had no menu entry. It now gets the Studio group with Python Studio.

          • The Database page offered a Python Console button to profiles without studio.python_console; the button now follows that key.
          • The Python console used dark-theme colours on SATOM's light pages (a pale pink error text on a pale pink panel, a grey output pane); it now uses the light theme's panels and the calibrated error red.
          • Translations: "Sandboxed (bubblewrap)" read in Spanish, French and Italian as the packing material ("burbuja de burlete", "bulle d'emballage", "imballaggio in bolle"); bubblewrap is the name of the sandbox and is no longer translated.

          • The concept-map coverage guard was red on main: the Update sources state feed (settings.update_sources_state) was neither mapped nor excluded.

          • Export left out the theme's logo and favicon, so a theme moved to another node arrived without its brand mark and nothing said so. The file is now schema satom.ui-theme/2 and carries both. Version 1 files still import.

          • The top-bar logo no longer stretches: a non-square upload keeps its proportions in the 28 px slot (object-fit: contain).
          • System backup bundles did not include data/branding/, even though docs/theming.md said they did. A restore onto a rebuilt node brought back every custom theme without its logo and favicon. Bundles now carry those files and a restore puts them back next to the theme rows. A bundle made before this change has no such folder and leaves the node's files alone.

          Security

          • Python Studio security review (asked for as "a security test, verify as well as you can that these scripts do not interfere with the confidentiality, availability, etc. of SATOM"). A static review of every Studio surface and an adversarial test on a running node found the following; all are fixed, each pinned by tests/test_studio_security.py. The resulting model is user guide §23.9.
          • A connection's secret could be sent anywhere by whoever may edit the connection: change its base URL (or OAuth2 token URL, or PostgreSQL host) to a server of their own and press Test. Changing the destination — scheme, host, port, authentication, header, token URL, user or TLS verification — now clears the stored secret, and the page says so.
          • No resource limits on the scripts and hooks runners: no memory or task cap and the run's work directory on the root disk, next to Postgres. A script that allocated, forked or wrote in a loop could take the node down. Both units now carry MemoryMax=1G, TasksMax=256, CPUQuota=200%, low CPU/IO weights and a 512 MB memory /tmp; inside the jail the root and /dev are read-only (bwrap's own root was a writable memory filesystem as large as half the host's RAM), a file is at most 256 MB, and the output is read with a cap instead of being buffered whole. The scripts queue holds at most 50 runs and run records are pruned after 30 days.
          • The Python console could exhaust the web service's memory: it runs in the web service, its jail had writable memory filesystems (/tmp, /, /dev/shm), its process cap counted every process of the service user (so it capped nothing), and its output was buffered whole. Now nothing in the jail is writable, a process may address 512 MiB, the run may add only a few tasks to the ones that exist, the output is read with a cap, and one console run at a time per node.
          • One template could freeze a web worker: Jinja's sandbox leaves ** and * alone and folds constants while compiling, so {{ 2 ** 99999999 }} or {{ 'a' * 10 ** 9 }} ran before any limit. Exponents above 64, results longer than 1 MiB, more than 1,000,000 loop items and rendered texts above 1 MiB are refused.
          • App operators could start unbounded work: runs per user (2) and per node (8) are capped, the Run button is rate-limited, run requests above 1 MiB are refused, lists filled from an API are cached for a minute, an action runs once per run and only on the version that produced it, and app runs are kept 90 days.
          • Operators could read data an app never showed them through the step details (a decision prints both values it compared); non-authors now see which steps ran and how they ended.
          • A form value in an API path could leave its segment (1?admin=1, %2e%2e/): inserted values are percent-encoded, encoded .///\ are refused and the query string is re-encoded.
          • An echoed credential reached the caller: answers are masked before a step, script or operator sees them (secret, Authorization value, Basic base64, OAuth2 token, JSON-escaped spellings). Password inputs are also masked in their urlencode/tojson/base64 spellings.
          • PostgreSQL "read only" could be walked out of with a statement list (COMMIT; SET …; COMMIT; DELETE …) and a result had no size limit: one statement through the extended protocol, read-only transaction AND session default, results capped at 8 MiB, a cancel if the server ignores the timeout, and require_auth=!password with libpq 16+.
          • HTTP calls had no total deadline (a server sending a byte at a time held the caller), and the other HA node was not on the refused list: both fixed.
          • Data stores had no size limit: 16 MiB and 20,000 rows per store, 128 KiB per row, 200 stores; writers of one store are serialised.
          • The connection broker and the egress proxy (outside the jail) started a thread per socket with no cap; now 8 and 32 at a time. The egress proxy no longer dials an address it refuses: link-local (cloud metadata) and HA node addresses got a TCP handshake before the refusal (found by the live test, where the metadata address timed out instead of being refused).
          • A run stopped by the memory limit now says so ("killed (SIGKILL): most often the memory limit…") instead of a bare exit code; the limit is a hard MemoryMax with no MemoryHigh throttle, which in the live test kept a runaway run stalled until its timeout. The units use OOMPolicy=continue and the jail runs at oom_score_adj 1000: in the live test systemd's default stopped the whole runner at the memory limit, with every other run in it, and left the run marked "running".

          • Six quick script runs stopped the Script Library for good (pre-existing, found by the live test): the runner starts once per queued request, and systemd's default start limit (5 in 10 s) failed the unit and its .path watcher, so no script ran again until someone ran systemctl reset-failed. Both runner units now have no start limit, and both runners move anything they cannot process out of their queue (to rejected/), so a stray file cannot make the watcher spin either.

          • Connections refuse dangerous destinations (found in this release's Connections before it shipped): a base URL, an OAuth2 token URL or a PostgreSQL host could point at this node's loopback services (the metrics store and the cache have no authentication), at the cloud metadata address or at any address of the node, and any user of an app could make SATOM call it — including by just opening a form whose list is filled from an API. Every call now resolves the host once, refuses it when any address is loopback, link-local, multicast, unspecified, reserved or this node's own, and dials the checked address (Host header and TLS server name keep the name). Internal (RFC 1918) addresses stay allowed. The OAuth2 token URL must be https (the client secret travels in it), and PostgreSQL no longer uses sslmode=prefer, which sends the password in clear to a server without TLS: verify-full against the trust store with TLS verification on, require with it off.

          • Theme SVGs are served under a sandbox Content-Security-Policy, so an SVG opened directly cannot run script even if the sanitiser misses something. The sanitiser now also removes unquoted event handlers, iframe, embed, object and external links.
